identity.purpose: Illustrate a prescribed fragment release and cloud stretching over the first three revolutions.

physics.model: Elliptic propagation with optional first-order secular J2 node, apsis and mean-anomaly rates. Release elements are treated as mean elements; short-period corrections are omitted. Direct deterministic evaluation at displayed elapsed time.
physics.incomingGeometry: Idealised circular encounter at 800 km and 72.5 degrees north, with inclinations 86.4 / 74 degrees. Inclinations and latitude are informed by NASA's published 2009 event analysis. These are synthetic circular states, not recovered historical ephemerides.
physics.sampleWeights: Equal representative weights, not physical masses or predicted fragment yield.
physics.randomAlgorithm: Mulberry32; uniform spherical direction from uniform z and azimuth; magnitude = cube root of a third uniform variate. Paired opposite vectors fill a ball uniformly in velocity space.

releaseSpeedMPerSecond.distribution: Uniform volume in the velocity ball, from zero to the selected maximum speed. Same relative magnitudes and directions on replay; no fitted breakup distribution.

physics.momentum: Equal-weight family means conserve total incoming linear momentum; paired kicks sum to zero.
physics.energy: Relative mean velocity contraction removes more kinetic energy than the kicks add throughout the allowed slider range.
physics.frame: Synthetic inertial Cartesian axes mapped to Three world (x,z,-y). Earth rotates about its polar axis at 7.292115e-5 rad/s, with arbitrary orientation at contact and no dated geographical claim.
physics.drawnEarth: Existing WGS84 ellipsoid and pinned Natural Earth geography. Experiment heights are above the spherical reference, distinct from WGS84 geodetic altitude.
excluded: Material fracture and calibrated size/mass spectra
Atmospheric drag and decay above the prescribed entry boundary
Short-period J2 corrections and higher gravity harmonics
Population-wide stochastic collisions, avoidance, collision probability and cascade timing

entryBoundary.rule: Remove on the first inbound radial crossing of a spherical R+120 km boundary. Reversible by seek; no atmospheric drag or lifetime estimate above this boundary.

secondary.source: First surviving primary sample at orbit 100 whose height is 500–1,200 km.
secondary.target: Synthetic circular orbit through the selected fragment position, tangential direction rotated 130 degrees from its transverse velocity. The target is propagated backwards from the specified encounter.
secondary.momentum: Paired kicks sum to zero about the combined mass-weighted centre-of-mass velocity; both incoming bodies are consumed at contact.
secondary.energy: Maximum kick is 0.7 sqrt(2 K_relative / total_mass), capped at 400 m/s; a filled velocity ball uses less than the available relative kinetic energy.
secondary.meaning: A controlled second breakup, not a probabilistically generated collision or a population-wide cascade prediction.

presentation.label: AN INDICATIVE SIMULATION
presentation.clock: Elapsed time from primary contact, with days/hours and original-orbit count. The scrubber follows the active guided sequence, including the optional secondary event. Playback stops at 500 original orbits.
presentation.guidedPace: 145-second primary sequence: slowed contact and young cloud; 3, 25, 100, 250 and 500 original orbits. Secondary mode adds a separately slowed encounter at orbit 100 and follows the new C cloud, giving a 183-second sequence. Native playback also offers 0.1, 1, 5 and 20 original orbits per real second. Both impacts have no constant-time hold. Positive harmonic-mean slopes join monotone cubic Hermite segments, making playback speed continuous across the cues; inverse seeking uses a bounded binary solve.
presentation.camera: Close on two illustrative bodies, hold the last 10 km camera distance for visible convergence; push into cloud A and follow its actual centroid for ten model minutes; continuously pull back to Earth from +10 to +40 minutes. Follow cloud retains the close camera; Frame Earth reveals the whole scene. Floating origin preserves local precision; positions are not exaggerated. The secondary branch uses the projectile and target positions for the approach and follows the C centroid after impact. Global framing fits the largest release apogee.
presentation.glyphs: Two authored 3D body diagrams before contact; 768 primary and 256 optional secondary irregular shaded shard glyphs after contact. Display sizes, rotation and body shapes are authored, not material-fracture outputs. Contact ring is a marker, not a fireball. 24 short model histories in the frame translating with the family mean release orbit reveal dispersion within cloud A; tips meet exact current fragment positions. Original orbit paths default off. Scale bar reports target-plane distance.
presentation.slider: Pauses at the displayed time; changes the maximum paired kick magnitude while holding seed, directions and relative magnitudes fixed; directly recomputes physical states and periods.
presentation.reducedMotion: Opening and replay stay paused. Later preference changes pause and never automatically restart.
presentation.navigation: Discover and cross-links distinguish the synthetic experiment from the retained catalogue chapter.
presentation.diagram: Linked Gabbard-style perigee/apogee against orbital period, coloured by primary A/B and secondary C. Future samples are hidden and removed/consumed samples dim. Heights are release-element quantities; J2 changes orientation rather than perigee/apogee.
presentation.startup: All scene materials and geometry/instance buffers receive a hidden warm render before the playback timestamp starts, including debris and histories that first appear at impact.

references.role: Primary reference for the two-body initial-state problem and elliptic Kepler equation; no SPICE code copied or runtime dependency.
Primary reference for Earth GM, reference radius and nominal rotation rate. Numerical constants only.
Primary NASA reference for first-order secular J2 rates. Edition-owned implementation; no copied code.

NASA analysis of the actual 2009 collision, including observed Gabbard diagrams and multidecade consequences. Context only: no historical satellite elements, figure images or digitised observations imported.

retained.factsUsed: 72.50 degree event latitude, 86.4 and 74 degree orbital inclinations; event context and Gabbard diagrams. No figure, image, spacecraft identity, orbital element set or digitised fragment record is reproduced.

references.role: Primary NASA context for catastrophic-impact specific energy and statistical breakup modelling. The conditional release here is not a complete Standard Breakup Model implementation.

rights.model: Edition-owned MIT code and synthetic initial conditions; no satellite records or licensed breakup dataset acquired.
rights.geography: Existing audited Natural Earth public-domain geometry is unchanged.
rights.context: Only factual numerical parameters and original mathematical implementation are published. Source PDFs are retained in ignored work storage; no NASA figures or third-party illustrations are redistributed. The authored synthetic model remains MIT; this does not relicense source reports.

validation.unit: Two-body energy/angular momentum and independent RK4 agreement through three orbits; J2 rate checks and independent Cartesian J2 integration of nodal drift over five days; deterministic 500-orbit seeks; first-entry boundary and reversal; conditioned secondary intersection, exact mass-weighted release momentum and energy budget, consumption and birth times; guided clock inversion for both branches; camera continuity and aspect adaptation. Positive continuous clock rates at all internal cues, strictly increasing frame samples through both impacts, and inverse-clock agreement are verified.
validation.browser: Slowed primary and secondary encounters; 500-orbit stop; orbit-per-second playback; seek/replay and seed retention; physical-time preservation on gestures; J2 and secondary controls; linked perigee/apogee plot; portrait/landscape and /zenit/ assets; no provider requests; actual young-cloud raster footprint. Consecutive rendered frames advance through both impacts; shader compilation is instrumented to ensure no shader is compiled when debris first appears.
validation.interpretation: Numerical validation of this authored two-body experiment, not empirical validation of fragmentation physics or a historical event.

review.reason: User requested hundreds of orbits, broader orbital divergence, and secondary collisions.
review.qualitativeLimits: 35 days of first-order gravity evolution, with an imposed entry boundary. No long-term lifetime or collision-frequency claim.
